reads_as_reason: Candidate is much calmer than the baseline, but the neckless block head on a wide slab chest, splayed mitten-ended arms and untapered column legs still read as an action figure or mannequin, not a finished adult product.

G1.evidence: Front and side clay views show the head sitting directly on the chest slab, with a visor-height block head and no visible neck (P2a FAIL, neck length 0.0759 hu). The shoulders are very wide (P3 FAIL, 0.4 of H) and the arms flare out into long tapered paddles. The legs are straight columns with no taper (P8a/P8b FAIL). Together these give a chunky mannequin look. The chibi-like head size is not the problem, since P1 passes at 0.145.

G2.evidence: The two-tone view has deliberate dark bands at waist, knee, ankle, elbow and wrist, which is the right idea. The silhouette itself is still stacked: a rectangular chest slab, a separate rounded-box pelvis with a dark band under it, then two parallel thigh columns that nearly fuse at the crotch. The side view has a large boxy pack hanging off the hip and arm zone, and the chest is also a stepped box. The front silhouette shows only a small armpit notch and no chest-waist-pelvis flow.

G3.evidence: The two-tone render uses matte white shells, graphite recesses and a glossy black visor, with no accent colour. Caveat: the rear view is not rendered two-tone (grey head and back), and the shell/dark boundaries are aliased with white speckles at the visor edge and on the left arm in the 3/4 view. Those are render artefacts and not a design fault.

G4.evidence: Head, chest, pelvis, thigh, shank and arm segments all use the same squircle-section, small-radius language, and joint bands are a consistent width. The pack box and the wedge foot are the only outliers, and both are visibly different from the rest. Caveat: this consistency is also what makes it look blocky.

G6.evidence: At equal height the candidate does not read as the same family as optimus_like or atlas_like. S2 IoU against them is 0.5366 and 0.5688. What matches: head height, hip and knee heights, and the overall standing A-pose. What does not match: shoulders and arms extend far outside both reference outlines (P3 FAIL), there is no neck or trapezius slope, the legs are not tapered (P8a/P8b FAIL), the feet are much longer (P10a FAIL), and the torso shows no waist taper beyond a small notch.

pairwise.evidence: Baseline (Image A) is a stack of unrelated boxes: shoulder boxes with horizontal ledges, a tiny neck cylinder under a flat-topped head, bulky stepped legs and mismatched foot blocks. The candidate has a coherent head, chest, pelvis and leg stack, tapered limbs, no stray ledges, and a two-tone view with deliberate dark joint bands and a visor. Neither is a finished product, but the candidate is clearly closer. The preference is stable regardless of presentation order.

top_changes.change: Narrow the shoulder line and arm span toward the references, and let the shoulder drop with a trapezius slope into a short visible neck. Bring the arms in closer to vertical.

Taper thigh and shank distally, with the widest point just below the hip. Narrow the knee and ankle sections, and open a visible gap between the thighs below the crotch. Add a real waist narrowing between chest and pelvis so the torso flows instead of reading as stacked slabs.
Shorten the foot and give it a lower, more tapered toe. Tuck or integrate the pack so the side profile does not show a large hanging box.

notes: I judged from the clay views, the silhouettes, the equal-height lineup and the two-tone render. I did not override any metric values. The rear two-tone view lacks the two-tone treatment, so I could not judge back-of-head and back-of-torso discipline. The sheet is labelled design-1 while the baseline is design-0, which matches the request. The visor and band aliasing is a render artefact. The camera is perspective, so the 3/4 views exaggerate arm width. Because of that I relied on the silhouettes and the metrics, which agree: P3, P2a, P8a/P8b and P10a all FAIL, in line with my G1, G2 and G6 verdicts.
